skeleton.finalText:
I wrote `src/index.ts`, and `npm run build` finishes with no errors. The build also produced `src/index.js`; I deleted it so that `src/index.ts` is the only file I added.

The contract is one function, `sweep(records, policy, runDate)`, because the spec doesn't describe anything with state:
- **Input:** it takes the records, the policy and the run date as parameters, so tests control the date.
- **Output:** it returns one `{ id, decision, reason }` per record, in input order.
- **Reasons:** the type allows only the spec's reasons: `"within period"`, `"expired"`, `"no policy"`, `` `hold:${string}` `` and `` `parent:${string}` ``.
- **Errors:** its doc comment says it throws an `Error` naming the record's id when the dates are impossible or a parent is missing. There are no custom error classes.

Three choices that both test suites and the implementation will depend on:
- **Field names:** I chose these myself; the spec doesn't name them. Records use `created`, `lastAccessed`, `holds`, `region` and `parentId`. The policy uses `categories` (keyed by category name, each with `periodDays` and `fromLastAccess`), `regions` (a list of `{ region, minimumDays }`) and `graceDays`.
- **Missing values:** `lastAccessed` and `parentId` can be left out or set to `null`, and both mean "none". I allowed both because the tests are plain JavaScript and either author might pass `null`.
- **Including `id` in each result:** the spec only asks for a decision and a reason. I added the id so tests can check results without relying on position alone.

Exports: `IsoDate`, `RetentionRecord`, `CategoryPolicy`, `RegionMinimum`, `RetentionPolicy`, `Decision`, `Reason`, `RecordDecision`, `sweep`

public.finalText:
I've written the test suite in three files under `tests/public/`, one for each Rule in the spec. `npm run build` reports no errors. Running the suite gives 29 failures, all from the `not implemented` stubs, as expected. Nothing outside `tests/public/` was changed, and I deleted the `.js` files the build produced.

- **`age.test.ts`**: `[happy-1]`, `[boundary-1]`, `[happy-2]`, `[boundary-2]`, `[boundary-3]`. These cover the exact days from the spec where a record moves from keep to flag to delete, a grace period of zero, ages counted from last access versus from creation (whether `lastAccessed` is missing or `null`), and region minimums. The region tests check a longer minimum, a region not in the list, and a minimum shorter than the period. The calendar-day tests use the 2024 leap day.
- **`holds-and-policies.test.ts`**: `[happy-3]`, `[unhappy-1]`, `[unhappy-2]`. These check that a record with several holds is kept for the first hold in sorted order, that an empty hold list counts as no hold, and that a record whose category isn't in the policy is kept with reason "no policy". They also check that each kind of impossible date makes the sweep fail with an error naming the record's id. The boundary case here is that a record created and last accessed on the run date itself is not refused.
- **`parents.test.ts`**: `[happy-4]`, `[boundary-4]`, `[unhappy-3]`. These check that a child of a held parent is kept, and that a child of a flagged or deleted parent follows its own age. Keeping passes down through grandchildren no matter how the input is ordered. A parent missing from the input makes the sweep fail with an error naming the child's id; a parent listed after its child is still found.

I left out cases the spec doesn't settle, so the tests don't push the developer toward a guess:
- a child whose parent is kept only because it is "within period";
- a record with both a hold and no policy;
- a held record that hasn't expired yet.

29 tests, in 3 files.

private.finalText:
I wrote 60 private tests in three files under `tests/private/`. `npm run build` reports no errors.

- **Against the stub:** all 60 fail, as they should.
- **Against a sketch implementation:** all 60 pass, along with the 29 public tests. I wrote that implementation in the scratchpad, outside the project.
- **Against public-tuned shortcuts:** I made four deliberately wrong versions of the sketch. All four pass every public test and each one fails at least one private test:
  - looking up a category as a plain object key, so `"constructor"` counts as having a policy;
  - taking the last hold in the list instead of the first when sorted;
  - checking last-accessed dates only in categories counted from last access;
  - passing a kept parent's decision down only one level.

What the private suite adds:

- **Age (`age.test.ts`):** other periods and grace periods, a grace period of one day, many records in input order, several categories in one policy, and empty input. Calendar-day checks cover non-leap years, the 2000 and 2100 century rules, month lengths, year end, a ten-year span, daylight-saving changes, and leap years when counting from last access. Region checks cover several listed regions, `"eu-west"` not matching `"eu"`, a minimum equal to the period, grace running from the minimum, and minimums on categories counted from last access.
- **Holds and policies (`holds-and-policies.test.ts`):** the first sorted hold appearing anywhere in the list, a held record inside the grace period, and categories named after built-in object properties or differing only in case. A record with impossible dates is refused even when it is held, has no policy, or is in a category counted from creation. Each refusal is checked to name the record's id.
- **Parents (`parents.test.ts`):** chains of 6 and 40 levels, keeping that starts halfway down a chain, a tree, every ordering of six records, and a record with a missing parent that is held, has no policy or is still within its period.

**One judgement call:** two tests treat a parent kept for being within its period, or for having no policy, the same as one kept by a hold, so its expired child is `keep` with `parent:<id>`. I read that from "Children follow a kept parent" and "A child of a kept record is kept." The scenario's example only shows a parent kept by a hold, so a stricter reading would make these two tests wrong.

**Left untested because the spec doesn't say:** cycles of parents, duplicate ids, which reason a kept child gets when it also has its own hold or is within its own period, hold versus "no policy" on the same record, and which id the error names when several records are invalid.

60 tests, in 3 files.

Open in the spec: none
